readme:
# OnlineJobs.ph Jobs Scraper

Scrape remote job posts from OnlineJobs.ph ([onlinejobs.ph](https://www.onlinejobs.ph/)), the job board where employers hire Filipino workers. You get the title, pay, work type, skills and posting time of every post, and the employer name where the post shows one. Turn on the job page option to add the full description, hours per week and the date the post was updated. Search by keyword and filter by work type.

## What you get

- One row per job post, with parsed pay numbers (from, up to, per hour, day, week or month) when the pay text is a clear number or range, and a posting time in ISO 8601.
- Optional job page details: the full description as HTML and plain text, hours per week and the date updated.
- Each post once per run, even when several keywords find it.
- A run with no input returns 5 posts for the keyword virtual assistant.

## Use with AI Agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client: Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom agents.

**Apify MCP server URL:**

`https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/onlinejobs-ph-jobs-scraper`

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `onlinejobs-ph-jobs-scraper` to find up to 5 jobs for the keyword "virtual assistant" (remote work for Filipino workers). Return results as a table with title, company, location and job URL."

Clients that support dynamic tool discovery (Claude.ai, VS Code) receive the full input schema automatically.

## Input

Every field is optional. Example:

```json
{
  "includeDetails": false,
  "maxResults": 5,
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 5,
  "searchQueries": [
    "virtual assistant"
  ]
}
```

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `searchQueries` | Keywords such as virtual assistant, video editor or bookkeeper. The site searches job titles and companies. Each keyword is its own search. |
| `workTypes` | Only posts of these work types: full time, part time or gig. Posts that accept any work type are kept. |
| `maxResultsPerQuery` | Posts per keyword. Default 50, up to 1000. |
| `maxResults` | Posts in total. 0 means no limit. |
| `includeDetails` | Read each job page for the extra fields. Default false. |

## Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Number at the end of the job address. It is the dedup key. |
| `title` | string | Job title as shown on the post. |
| `employer_name` | string, null | Employer name when the post shows a logo with a name. Most posts hide the employer. |
| `employer_id` | string, null | Number of the employer in the logo address. Only posts with a logo carry it. |
| `employer_logo` | string, null | Logo image URL of the post, when it has one. |
| `work_type` | string, null | Badge of the post: Any, Full Time, Part Time or Gig. |
| `salary_text` | string, null | Wage text exactly as the employer wrote it, for example $5 per hour or tbd. |
| `salary_min` | number, null | Lower bound read from the pay text, only when the text is a clear number or range. |
| `salary_max` | number, null | Upper bound read from the pay text. Empty for open-ended pay such as 500+. |
| `salary_currency` | string, null | Currency code read from the pay text. A plain dollar sign is read as USD. |
| `salary_period` | string, null | hour, day, week, biweekly, month or year, read from the pay text. |
| `hours_per_week` | string, null | Hours per week as the employer wrote it. Needs the job page. |
| `posted_text` | string, null | Posting time text of the result list (Philippine time). |
| `date_posted` | string, null | Posting time as ISO 8601 UTC. |
| `date_updated` | string, null | Date the post was last updated (ISO date). Needs the job page. |
| `snippet` | string, null | First lines of the description, as shown in the result list. |
| `skills` | array | Skill tags of the post. |
| `skill_slugs` | array | Skill categories of the post as the site names them (category--skill). |
| `description_html` | string, null | Full description as HTML. Needs the job page. |
| `description_text` | string, null | Full description as plain text. Needs the job page. |
| `job_url` | string | Address of the job post. |
| `details_fetched` | boolean | True when the job page was read for this row. |
| `search_query` | string | The keyword that found the post, or all jobs. |
| `source` | string | Site host. |
| `scraped_at` | string | Time of the scrape, ISO 8601 UTC. |

Fields that a post does not show are `null`. The list shows 30 posts per page. Fields marked as coming from the job page are `null` when `includeDetails` is off. The site shows the employer only on posts that carry a logo, and keeps contact and apply data behind a jobseeker login, so none of that is in the data.

## Pricing

This Actor uses pay per event. There is a small `apify-actor-start` event when a run starts and one `job-result` event for each post in the dataset. You are never charged for a post twice, and a run stops when it reaches the maximum charge you set.

Price: $0.001 start fee per run, then $0.0015 per job result ($1.50 per 1,000 jobs).

## FAQ

**Why is the employer empty for most posts?**
OnlineJobs.ph hides the employer name from visitors who are not logged in. Only posts with a company logo show a name, taken from the logo text, and `employer_id` comes from the logo address.

**How is the pay read?**
`salary_text` is always the text the employer wrote, for example "$5 per hour" or "tbd". The numeric fields are filled only when the text is a clear number or range. A plain dollar sign is read as USD, and amounts with a plus sign or the word above only get `salary_min`. Texts such as "Based on Experience" give no numbers.

**Is the posting time exact?**
Yes. The result list carries the posting time to the second. `posted_text` is the Philippine time as the site shows it and `date_posted` is the same moment in UTC.

**What happens when a keyword finds nothing?**
The run ends normally with the status "0 jobs found for <keyword>." and nothing is charged.
